name: Rolex
tagline: The crown of watchmaking, and the world's most recognised luxury watch.
summary: Rolex is the best-known luxury watch brand in the world, famous for robust, precise and instantly recognisable sport and dress watches. It is owned by a private foundation and makes almost every component in-house.
history:
Rolex was founded in London in 1905 by Hans Wilsdorf and his brother-in-law Alfred Davis as Wilsdorf & Davis, importing Swiss movements and fitting them in cases sold by jewellers. Wilsdorf registered the name Rolex in 1908, a word short enough to fit on a dial and easy to say in any language. High British taxes after the First World War led the company to move to Geneva in 1919.

The brand's reputation rests on firsts. In 1914 a Rolex was the first wristwatch to earn a Class A precision certificate from the Kew Observatory. In 1926 it patented the Oyster, a waterproof case, and in 1927 swimmer Mercedes Gleitze wore one across the English Channel. The Perpetual self-winding rotor followed in 1931, and the Datejust, the first self-winding wristwatch with a date in a window, in 1945.

The post-war decades produced the icons: the Explorer and Submariner in 1953, the GMT-Master in 1955, the Day-Date in 1956 and the Cosmograph Daytona in 1963. When Wilsdorf died in 1960 the company was already held by the Hans Wilsdorf Foundation, which still owns it. Rolex came through the quartz crisis by staying mechanical and raising its prices, and today it is by far the largest Swiss watch brand by revenue. In 2023 it bought its long-time retailer Bucherer.
knownFor: The Submariner, Daytona and the Oyster case
innovations: 1926: Oyster, the first waterproof wristwatch case
1945: Datejust, first self-winding wristwatch with a date window
2015: Superlative Chronometer standard of -2/+2 seconds a day
funFacts: Rolex is owned by a charitable foundation and pays no dividends to shareholders.
Paul Newman's own Daytona sold for $17.8 million in 2017.
A Deepsea Special strapped to the Trieste bathyscaphe reached the bottom of the Mariana Trench in 1960.

name: Patek Philippe
tagline: You never actually own one; you merely look after it for the next generation.
summary: Patek Philippe is widely seen as the finest watch manufacture in the world. It is family-owned in Geneva and famous for grand complications, the Calatrava and the Nautilus, and it holds most of the auction records in the field.
history:
Polish émigré Antoni Patek and watchmaker François Czapek began making pocket watches in Geneva in 1839. In 1844 Patek met Jean Adrien Philippe, inventor of the keyless crown-winding system, and in 1851 the company became Patek Philippe & Co. Royal clients, including Queen Victoria, established its reputation early.

The firm made what is thought to be the first Swiss wristwatch in 1868, for Countess Koscowicz of Hungary. The Great Depression brought it close to collapse, and in 1932 the Stern brothers, who supplied its dials, bought the company. Under the Sterns Patek introduced the Calatrava in 1932 and a long run of perpetual calendars, chronographs and minute repeaters. The Henry Graves Supercomplication, finished in 1933, stayed the most complicated watch in the world for more than 50 years.

Patek resisted the quartz trend and in 1976 launched the Gérald Genta-designed Nautilus, which became its most sought-after model. The Patek Philippe Seal replaced the Geneva Seal in 2009 with an even stricter in-house standard. Thierry Stern, the fourth generation of the family, runs the company today and keeps production deliberately scarce.

timeline.event: Founded in Geneva as Patek, Czapek & Co.
Stern family acquires the company; Calatrava launched
Calibre 89, the most complicated portable timepiece of its day

funFacts: The Henry Graves Supercomplication sold for about $24 million in 2014.
Patek keeps a workshop that can service every watch it has made since 1839.
Its 'Generations' advertising campaign has run since 1996.

name: Seiko
tagline: Japan's watchmaking giant, from $100 divers to Grand Seiko masterpieces.
summary: Seiko is one of the few fully vertically integrated watchmakers in the world, making everything from hairsprings to quartz crystals. It introduced the first quartz wristwatch and makes excellent value dive watches as well as refined high-end pieces.
history:
Kintaro Hattori opened a watch and jewellery shop in Tokyo's Ginza district in 1881. In 1892 he started the Seikosha factory to make wall clocks, and in 1913 it produced the Laurel, Japan's first wristwatch. The 1923 Great Kanto earthquake destroyed the factory, but Hattori rebuilt it, and in 1924 the first watches bearing the Seiko name went on sale.

After the war Seiko modernised quickly. It began competing in Swiss observatory chronometry trials in the 1960s, was the official timekeeper of the 1964 Tokyo Olympics, and launched its first diver's watch in 1965. Grand Seiko began in 1960 as an attempt to make the best watch possible.

On Christmas Day 1969 Seiko released the Astron, the world's first quartz wristwatch. Quartz changed the industry and nearly destroyed traditional Swiss watchmaking. Seiko went on to develop Kinetic and, in 1999, Spring Drive, which combines a mainspring with quartz regulation. In 2017 Grand Seiko became a separate brand, and Seiko today spans everything from affordable Seiko 5 automatics to Credor haute horlogerie.
ownership: Public (Seiko Group Corporation), Hattori family influence
knownFor: First quartz watch, legendary affordable divers
innovations: 1969: Astron, the world's first quartz wristwatch

timeline.event: Kintaro Hattori opens his shop in Ginza

funFacts: 'Seiko' roughly means 'exquisite' or 'success' in Japanese.
A Seiko 6139 was the first automatic chronograph worn in space, in 1973.
Seiko grows its own quartz crystals.

name: Casio
tagline: Indestructible G-Shocks and the digital watches that defined an era.
summary: Casio is a Japanese electronics company whose watches range from the $20 F-91W to high-end G-Shock MR-G models. The G-Shock made shock resistance a cultural phenomenon, and Casio is one of the best-selling watch brands in the world.
history:
Tadao Kashio founded Kashio Seisakujo in Tokyo in 1946, and with his brothers he built the Casio 14-A in 1957, the world's first compact, fully electric calculator. Calculators made Casio famous, and its electronics expertise led naturally to watches.

The Casiotron, launched in 1974, was one of the first digital watches with an automatic calendar. In 1983 engineer Kikuo Ibe released the G-Shock DW-5000C after testing prototypes by throwing them out of a third-floor window. It was built on the principle of 'triple ten': a 10-metre drop, 10 bar of water resistance and a 10-year battery.

The F-91W of 1989 became one of the best-selling watches ever made. G-Shock grew into a global streetwear and skate culture icon in the 1990s, and Casio has added solar power, radio-controlled timekeeping, Bluetooth and the premium MR-G line. More than 100 million G-Shocks had been shipped by 2017.
funFacts: Kikuo Ibe tested G-Shock prototypes by dropping them from a third-floor bathroom window.
The F-91W has been estimated to sell around 3 million units a year.
G-Shock's 'triple ten' goal: 10 m drop, 10 bar, 10-year battery.

name: Nomos Glashütte
tagline: Bauhaus clarity with in-house movements from Saxony.
summary: Nomos Glashütte is a young manufacture from Germany's historic watch town, known for clean, modernist designs and in-house movements at accessible prices. The Tangente is one of the most recognisable modern dress watches.
history:
Roland Schwertner founded Nomos in January 1990, just weeks after the fall of the Berlin Wall, in Glashütte, the Saxon town that had been the heart of German watchmaking before the war and was turned into a state-owned combine under East German rule.

Its first four models, Tangente, Orion, Ludwig and Tetra, appeared in 1992 and were built on modified ETA/Peseux manual movements. The designs drew on the Bauhaus and the Deutscher Werkbund: sans-serif numerals, thin hands and a lot of space on the dial.

Nomos soon started building its own movements. In 2005 it released its first in-house calibre, and in 2014 it introduced the DUW 3001 automatic and its own swing system, the 'Nomos swing system', which makes it one of the few makers of this size to produce its own escapement. It remains independent and designs its watches with Berlin Weinberg studio, winning many design awards.
innovations: 2005: First in-house movement, Alpha family expanded
2014: Nomos swing system, an in-house escapement
2015: DUW 3001, one of the thinnest automatic movements at its price

timeline.event: Founded in Glashütte after German reunification

funFacts: Nomos makes its own escapement, which is rare for a brand of its size.
Nomos sometimes paints its dials in unusual colours that sell out immediately.
The Nomos name was borrowed from a short-lived Glashütte watch company of the early 1900s.

name: Apple
tagline: The world's best-selling watch, and a computer on your wrist.
summary: The Apple Watch, launched in 2015, quickly became the world's best-selling wristwatch, outselling the entire Swiss watch industry by units. It combines health sensors, fitness tracking and iPhone integration.
history:
Apple was founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne in California. It was not a watch company for nearly four decades. Under Tim Cook, and with design led by Jony Ive, Apple announced the Apple Watch in September 2014 and released it in April 2015, including a $10,000-plus solid gold Edition model aimed at the luxury market.

The gold models were quietly dropped, and Apple instead focused on health and fitness: an ECG app, fall detection, blood oxygen sensing and crash detection. Sales grew quickly, and by 2019 Apple was estimated to ship more watches each year than the entire Swiss watch industry.

The rugged Apple Watch Ultra followed in 2022 for divers, runners and hikers. With the Hermès collaboration and a large accessory ecosystem, Apple has made the smartwatch a mainstream product and put real pressure on entry-level traditional watches.
knownFor: The best-selling watch in the world
innovations: 2015: Digital Crown for navigating a smartwatch
2018: FDA-cleared ECG in a consumer watch
2022: Apple Watch Ultra dive computer features

timeline.event: Series 4 adds ECG and fall detection
Estimated to outsell the Swiss watch industry

funFacts: The 2015 Apple Watch Edition in 18k gold cost up to $17,000.
Apple Watch has been credited with detecting heart conditions in thousands of users.
The Digital Crown is a nod to traditional watch crowns.

name: MB&F
tagline: Horological Machines: kinetic sculpture for the wrist.
summary: MB&F (Maximilian Büsser & Friends) is an independent Geneva creative lab that builds avant-garde 'Horological Machines' shaped like spaceships, frogs and jellyfish, alongside more traditional 'Legacy Machines'. Each piece is a collaboration with independent craftsmen.
history:
Maximilian Büsser spent seven years at Jaeger-LeCoultre and then revived Harry Winston's watch division, where he started the celebrated Opus series of collaborations with independent watchmakers. In 2005 he left to found MB&F, an artistic and micro-engineering laboratory built around small teams of 'friends'.

The first watch, HM1 of 2007, had a figure-of-eight case, four barrels and a central tourbillon. Later Horological Machines took the idea further: HM3 'Frog', HM5 inspired by 1970s supercars, HM6 'Space Pirate' and the domed HM10 'Bulldog'. In 2011 the Legacy Machine line reimagined 19th-century pocket watches with dramatic balance wheels floating above the dial.

MB&F also opened the M.A.D.Gallery in Geneva for mechanical art. It won the top prize, the Aiguille d'Or, at the GPHG in 2019 for the LM Flying T, and in 2022 it launched the M.A.D.1, a more affordable watch sold through a lottery. It produces only a few hundred pieces a year.
innovations: 2007: HM1, a figure-of-eight case with four barrels
2011: Legacy Machine with a suspended balance
2019: LM Flying T wins the GPHG Aiguille d'Or

timeline.event: LM Flying T wins the Aiguille d'Or

funFacts: The name stands for Maximilian Büsser & Friends, a nod to the independent craftsmen credited on every machine.
Its M.A.D.1 was allocated by random draw to keep flippers out.
The HM3 'Frog' has domes for eyes that display the hours and minutes.

name: Timex
tagline: It takes a licking and keeps on ticking.
summary: Timex is America's most famous everyday watch brand, with roots going back to 1854 in Connecticut. It democratised the wristwatch with cheap, tough designs and made the Ironman, one of the best-selling sports watches ever.
history:
Timex traces its roots to the Waterbury Clock Company, founded in 1854 in Connecticut's Naugatuck Valley, which was known as the 'Switzerland of America'. Waterbury made inexpensive clocks and the famous dollar pocket watches sold by Ingersoll, and it supplied wristwatches to American soldiers in the First World War.

After the Depression the company was bought by Norwegian investors Thomas Olsen and Joakim Lehmkuhl, who used its factories to make fuses during the Second World War. In 1950 it launched the Timex brand, cheap and robust watches built with hard alloy bearings instead of jewels. Its legendary 'torture test' TV adverts with John Cameron Swayze made it America's best-selling watch, and by the 1960s one in every two watches sold in the US was a Timex.

Timex adapted to quartz and digital watches, launched the Indiglo backlight in 1992 and the Ironman Triathlon in 1986, which became the best-selling sports watch in the United States. Today it is part of the Timex Group, still owned by the Olsen family, and has found new fans with heritage reissues such as the Marlin and Q Timex.
knownFor: The Ironman, Indiglo and affordable reliability
innovations: 1950: Hard-alloy bearings replace jewels for cheap, durable watches
funFacts: Timex's TV ads strapped watches to boat propellers and horses' hooves.
Bill Clinton wore a Timex Ironman at his inauguration.
Indiglo was used during the 2001 World Trade Center evacuation to help people navigate stairwells.
